faq.q: Can I watch the polo final from the boat?

Many guests prefer docking at Sotogrande Marina (walking distance to the club) or at nearby Puerto de Sotogrande.

faq.q: What's included in the charter price?

faq.q: How far in advance should I book for the polo final?

data.body_html:
Planning to attend the Sotogrande Polo Final 2042? Renting a boat from Marbella is the smartest way to combine world-class polo with a day on the Mediterranean. This guide covers everything you need to know – from boat options and prices to routes and booking tips – so you can arrive in style and skip the traffic.

Why choose a boat for the Sotogrande Polo Final?

The Sotogrande Polo Final is one of the most anticipated events on the Costa del Sol social calendar. Held at the Santa María Polo Club, it attracts a glamorous crowd. Driving from Marbella can take over an hour, and parking is a nightmare. By boat, you avoid the congestion and turn the journey into a highlight. You'll cruise past Marbella's Golden Mile, the dunes of Cabopino, and the cliffs of Cala del Faro before arriving at Sotogrande Marina – just a short walk from the polo fields.

Distance and travel time from Marbella to Sotogrande

Puerto Banús to Sotogrande is approximately 40 nautical miles. At an average cruising speed of 20–25 knots, expect a 2-hour journey each way. For a full day, an 8-hour charter gives you ample time to travel, enjoy the polo, and return. If you prefer a shorter trip, consider a 4-hour charter and dock at Sotogrande for the final hours of the match.

Boat options for your Sotogrande polo trip

Our fleet departs exclusively from Puerto Banús. Here are the best options for polo day:

  • Astondoa 40 – 12.5m, 9 pax. Ideal for small groups. From €749/2h or €2,299/8h.
  • Azimut 39 – 12.5m, 11 pax. Spacious and fast. Same pricing as Astondoa.
  • Mangusta 80 (white or grey) – 24m, 12 pax. Flagship experience with jet ski included. €4,719 for 4h minimum.
  • Azimut 58 Flybridge – 17.6m, 12 pax. Great deck space for socialising.
  • Pershing 46 – 14m, 10 pax. Sporty and elegant.

For other boats (Fairline Targa, Ferretti 94, Canados 86, K80, etc.) pricing is on request – contact us via WhatsApp for a tailored quote.

Pricing and inclusions

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden extras.

Best route and stops along the way

Leave Puerto Banús heading south. Pass by the luxurious villas of the Golden Mile and the beach clubs of Río Verde. Just before Estepona, you'll find the secluded coves of Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés – perfect for a morning swim or a champagne toast. Continue past Estepona's marina and the dunes of Cabopino, then enter the Sotogrande estuary. Dock at Sotogrande Marina, where the polo club is a short walk (or a 5-minute taxi) away.

What to expect at the Sotogrande Polo Final 2042

The final is typically held in August, with gates opening mid-morning. Expect a day of high-goal polo, champagne, and fashion. Dress code is smart-casual; boat shoes are fine for the marina. After the match, you can head back to your boat for a relaxing cruise home as the sun sets over the Mediterranean.

Booking tips and recommendations

Book early – August is peak season. We recommend reserving your boat 2–3 months in advance. For groups of up to 12, the Mangusta 80 offers the most impressive experience. For smaller groups, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 are cost-effective and comfortable. Always confirm your departure time with the skipper to align with the polo schedule.
